Snapshot anchor — the `kind=\"snapshot\"` record + head v2 fields\n30\t\n31\tTwo coupled owner-signed commitments, cross-checked; the **head is authority**, the record is the durable, replayable intent.\n32\t\n33\t**(A) A spine record `kind=\"snapshot\"`, `actor=\"OWNER\"`**, appended at the LIVE tip `S=T+1` via the normal retain-all path (real `cert_digest` over content, `entry_hash`, `fsync`-before-ack) *before any deletion*, so it is itself hash-chained and covered by every future head. Add `\"snapshot\"` to `KINDS` in `spine/models.py`. Payload commits, over the pruned prefix `[0..K)`:\n34\t\n35\t| field | value |\n36\t|---|---|\n37\t| `base_seq` | `K` — first RETAINED seq = `first_seq` of the oldest KEPT sealed segment (**K MUST be a sealed-segment boundary** so we archive whole segments and `base_prev_hash` is already a stored value) |\n38\t| `base_prev_hash` | `entry_hash(K-1)` = boundary_hash of the newest archived segment = the kept segment's existing `first_prev_hash` — the synthetic genesis-prev the re-based live set links from |\n39\t| `base_count` | absolute count of pruned records `[0..K)` (`==K` when contiguous from genesis; both stored and cross-checked) |\n40\t| `delta_merkle_root` | binary Merkle over **this prune's** new leaves `[entry_hash(K_prev)..entry_hash(K-1)]`, seq order, dup-last-on-odd (C2) |\n41\t| `cumulative_merkle_root` | `H(prior_snapshot.cumulative_merkle_root ‖ delta_merkle_root)` — the running accumulator so prune #N never needs the offline archive mounted |\n42\t| `snapshot_seq` | `S` (its own seq) |\n43\t| `prev_snapshot_seq` | prior snapshot's seq (`-1` first) — the snapshot meta-chain, cross-checked against the head meta-chain |\n44\t| `folded_state` | the cumulative `SnapshotState` (§6), computed as `fold(load(prior_snapshot), delta_records)` |\n45\t\n46\t**(B) `SignedChainHead` v2** copies the SAME six commit fields (`base_seq, base_prev_hash, base_count, cumulative_merkle_root, snapshot_seq, prev_head_hash`) INSIDE the owner-Ed25519 payload; `head_hash=entry_hash(S)`, `last_seq=S`, `entry_count = base_count + len(live)` (stays **ABSOLUTE**). The head — not the record — is the verification authority; the record is what the reconciler replays.\n47\t\n48\t**Descends from exactly one prior head:** `prev_head_hash = sha256_hex(evidence_signing_bytes(_head_payload(prior_accepted_head)))`. A verifier accepts head `H` iff `sha256(signing_bytes(H)) == floor.head_sig_hash` (re-verify the current accepted head) **OR** `H.prev_head_hash == floor.head_sig_hash` (advance to its unique child). A linear meta-chain = exactly one parent, no fork, no skip, no replay of a stale owner-signed head. `classify_head` additionally cross-checks `head.{base_seq,base_count,cumulative_merkle_root} == prev_snapshot_seq` chain consistency; because `snapshot_seq` is in the *signed* head, the head can never claim a boundary the immutable record does not carry.\n49\t\n50\t---\n51\t\n52\t## 2. Head-schema v2 migration (A1) — the flag-day linchpin\n53\t\n54\t`SignedChainHead` (`models.py:56`, keep `extra=\"forbid\"`) gains six fields defaulted to the **no-prune identity**:\n55\t\n56\t```python\n57\tbase_seq: int = 0\n58\tbase_prev_hash: str = _GENESIS_PREV\n59\tbase_count: int = 0\n60\tcumulative_merkle_root: str = \"\"\n61\tsnapshot_seq: int = -1\n62\tprev_head_hash: str = \"\"\n63\t# schema_version bumps 1 -> 2 only at the FIRST prune, and STAYS 2 thereafter\n64\t```\n65\t\n66\t**THE blocking gate — version-conditional signing payload** in `_head_payload` (`chain.py:50`, currently `model_dump(mode=\"json\")` minus `signatures`, and `canonical_json` sorts keys):\n67\t\n68\t```python\n69\tdef _head_payload(head):\n70\t    d = head.model_dump(mode=\"json\")\n71\t    d.pop(\"signatures\", None)\n72\t    if d.get(\"schema_version\", 1) < 2:          # explicit pop — NOT exclude_unset\n73\t        for f in (\"base_seq\", \"base_prev_hash\", \"base_count\",\n74\t                  \"cumulative_merkle_root\", \"snapshot_seq\", \"prev_head_hash\"):\n75\t            d.pop(f, None)\n76\t    return d\n77\t```\n78\t\n79\tA v1-signed head re-dumped under the v2 model then produces **byte-identical** signing bytes — every persisted `head.json` and every old-client verify passes unchanged. `sign_head`/`verify_head` both route through `_head_payload`, so v1/v2 stay symmetric. **Merge gate: a real pre-existing v1 head verifies byte-identically under the v2 model.**\n80\t\n81\t**After the fleet upgrade, once the first prune emits a v2 head, ALL subsequent heads are v2** (routine `sigil sign` too) so they carry `prev_head_hash` and keep `base_*` current — otherwise the meta-chain breaks between prunes.\n82\t\n83\t**Harden the two readers:**\n84\t- `verify_checkpoint` (`checkpoint.py:86`, bare `model_validate_json` — today crashes a v1 client on v2 fields): wrap `model_validate_json + classify_head` in `try/except`; on `ValidationError`/parse failure do a lenient `json.loads` to read `schema_version` — if it exceeds the known max return the DISTINCT `(False, \"schema too new — upgrade sigil\")`; a genuinely corrupt head returns `(False, \"corrupt head\")`. Never silent, never false-clean.\n85\t- `SpineTailer._resolve_head` (swallows all exceptions to `(None,None)` = \"un-notarized\" = a false-CLEAN degrade): peek `schema_version` first; if `> SUPPORTED`, return a THIRD sentinel `\"schema_ahead\"` that `poll()`/`check_anchor` surface as `anchor_ok=False, upgrade_required=True` — never the benign \"un-notarized live tail.\"\n86\t\n87\t**Old mobile client vs a v2 head:** `extra=\"forbid\"` → `ValidationError` → routed to \"upgrade required\" (SAFE: not-proven, never false-clean). **The first prune is a fleet-upgrade FLAG DAY** — gate v2-head emission behind every paired mesh device advertising `max_head_schema >= 2` (piggyback `mesh/registry.capability_map`), plus explicit owner sign-off.\n88\t\n89\t---\n90\t\n91\t## 3. verify_chain / classify_head / verify_head snapshot-awareness\n92\t\n93\t**`verify_chain` (`chain.py:37`)** gains `genesis_prev: str = _GENESIS_PREV` and seeds `prev = genesis_prev` instead of the hardcoded constant. Every existing caller passes the default → byte-identical. The `i>0` seq-contiguity check (`chain.py:44`) is unchanged; a re-based live segment whose first record has `prev_hash == base_prev_hash` links cleanly instead of forking.\n94\t\n95\t**`verify_head` (`chain.py:66`)** gains `genesis_prev` passthrough and becomes base-aware. Replace line 73's `head.entry_count != len(entries)` with:\n96\t```python\n97\tif head.head_hash != exp_hash or head.last_seq != exp_seq \\\n98\t   or head.entry_count != head.base_count + len(entries):\n99\t    return False, \"head does not match the chain (log truncated or head rewritten)\"\n100\t```\n101\t(reuse the existing `prev_highwater` param for the floor high-water check — it is already there).\n102\t\n103\t**`classify_head` (`checkpoint.py:65`)** becomes snapshot-aware and selects the live window **BY SEQ, not array prefix**:\n104\t```python\n105\tbase = head.base_count\n106\tsigned_live = head.entry_count - base\n107\tlive = [e for e in entries if e.seq >= head.base_seq]\n108\t# LEFT-EDGE PIN — UNCONDITIONAL TAMPERING (closes the false-CLEAN front-drop hole):\n109\tif not live or live[0].seq != head.base_seq or live[0].prev_hash != head.base_prev_hash:\n110\t    return False, \"TAMPERING: live window does not start at the signed base (front-truncated/rolled back)\"\n111\t# ANTI-TRUNCATION — the real guard that survives pruning (NOT the no-op n<entry_count):\n112\tif len(live) < signed_live:\n113\t    return False, f\"TAMPERING: live window has {len(live)} records but the head anchors {signed_live} (truncated)\"\n114\tok, msg = verify_head(head, live[:signed_live], tr, genesis_prev=head.base_prev_hash)\n115\tif not ok:\n116\t    return False, f\"TAMPERING: history rewritten at or below the signed head — {msg}\"\n117\tif len(live) > signed_live:\n118\t    return True, f\"anchors {signed_live} live records; {len(live)-signed_live} appended since — run `sigil sign`\"\n119\treturn True, f\"anchors all {signed_live} live records (current)\"\n120\t```\n121\t`entry_count` stays ABSOLUTE; `base_count` is inside the owner-signed payload and Merkle-bound to exactly `base_count` archived leaves, so an attacker cannot shrink the live window and mask it by inflating `base_count` without an owner signature. Records at `seq < base_seq` still physically present during a crash cutover window are the benign not-yet-pruned prefix — ignored by the by-seq selection, so no crash state reads as TAMPERING.\n122\t\n123\t**Unkeyed paths (required, else the pruned store false-tampers in `sigil verify`/dashboard/mobile feed):** `store.verify()` and `SpineTailer` seed `genesis_prev` from the manifest's advisory `base_prev_hash` (cross-checked against the signed head so the advisory field is never trust-bearing); `SpineTailer` seeds `_last_hash = base_prev_hash` when resuming from a cursor `since_seq < base_seq` (else the first live record reads as a linkage break).\n124\t\n125\t---\n126\t\n127\t## 4. Durable external floor (C1) — `floor.json` contract\n128\t\n129\t`~/.sigil/floor.json`, mode `0600`, at `SIGIL_HOME` root **OUTSIDE `spine/`** so `SpineStore.reset()` / `sigil ingest --reset` (which `rmtree`s the spine dir) can never lower it. Written only via `atomicio.atomic_write_text` (temp→fsync→replace→dir-fsync), and only after a head+manifest have committed.\n130\t\n131\t```jsonc\n132\t{ \"schema_version\": 1,\n133\t  \"scope\": \"<SCOPE>\",\n134\t  \"last_seq\": <int>,            // monotonic up\n135\t  \"base_seq\": <int>,            // monotonic up\n136\t  \"base_count\": <int>,          // monotonic up\n137\t  \"head_sig_hash\": \"<sha256 of the CURRENT accepted head's signing bytes>\",\n138\t  \"updated_ts\": \"<iso>\" }\n139\t```\n140\t\n141\t**Reject rules** (in `classify_head`/`verify_checkpoint`, mirrored into `SpineTailer._high_water`): reject any head/snapshot with `last_seq < floor.last_seq` (rollback), `base_count < floor.base_count` or `base_seq < floor.base_seq` (un-prune / older-snapshot replay), or a v2 head failing the meta-chain rule of §1(B). **Update is upward-only**, after the commit instant (§9-B2); a legitimate `--reset` shortening the spine requires a **separate, explicit, owner-key-gated `sigil floor reset`**, never the routine reset.\n142\t\n143\t**Honest limit:** closed for warm / same-host / returning-paired verifiers by the persisted floor + `SpineTailer._high_water`. **Unclosable from data alone** for a cold verifier bootstrapping off an untrusted mirror — the owner key is FS-resident (`checkpoint.py:9`, accepted §1.3 simplification), so a full-tuple rollback `{short spine, re-signed v2 head, rolled-back floor, matching snapshot}` is class-identical to today's single-file rollback, **not widened**. Bounded (not eliminated) by seeding the initial floor over the authenticated WireGuard pairing channel, never the mirror (§10).\n144\t\n145\t---\n146\t\n147\t## 5. Cold-archive move + live re-base + verifier re-attach\n148\t\n149\t**Which moves:** whole sealed segments only (never the active, never a partial), oldest-first, whose `last_seq < K`, keeping the newest `N` sealed live (`SIGIL_SPINE_LIVE_SEALED`, default keep ≥2 for the warm window) or those younger than a retention window — and only up to the referential floor (§7). **MOVE = copy → verify → drop** (additive-then-atomic; never a destructive rename first).\n150\t\n151\t**Archive layout** — `SIGIL_HOME/spine/archive/` (relocatable to an offline mount via `SIGIL_SPINE_ARCHIVE_DIR`):\n152\t```\n153\tarchive/segments/seg-*.jsonl.gz          # moved segments, still gzip, byte-identical\n154\tarchive/archive.manifest.json            # APPEND-ONLY across prunes, generation-stamped\n155\t```\n156\t`archive.manifest.json` = one entry per archived segment `{id, file, first_seq, last_seq, first_prev_hash, boundary_hash, sha256, count}` + one entry per snapshot `{snapshot_seq, base_seq, base_count, delta_merkle_root, cumulative_merkle_root, prev_head_hash, head_sig_hash}`. It is a genesis-rooted segment set: `seg-0.first_prev_hash == _GENESIS_PREV`, each `boundary_hash == next.first_prev_hash`, last `boundary_hash == base_prev_hash`.\n157\t\n158\t**Live manifest re-base:** the retain-all `Manifest` gains reserved header fields `base_seq/base_prev_hash/base_count/snapshot_seq/cumulative_merkle_root` (advisory — manifest stays non-load-bearing). The re-based manifest (`generation++`) drops the archived segments; the oldest REMAINING live segment keeps its existing `first_prev_hash` (already `== base_prev_hash` — a whole-segment boundary), so **no segment file is rewritten** — pure metadata.\n159\t\n160\t**Re-attach to verify from genesis:** `sigil spine verify --with-archive <dir>` concatenates `archive/segments…` (in `archive.manifest` order) then the live segments in seq order → one genesis-rooted stream → `verify_chain(genesis_prev=_GENESIS_PREV)`; then recompute each `delta_merkle_root` from the real archived leaves and re-chain the accumulator, asserting `== each snapshot's committed cumulative_merkle_root`. Full genesis→tip integrity for anyone handed the archive. Per-segment `sha256` is the at-rest integrity; the owner keeps ≥1 replica (losing the archive makes the pruned prefix unrecoverable — only the Merkle commitment proves what *was* there).\n161\t\n162\t---\n163\t\n164\t## 6. State-folding — `SnapshotState` + per-bearer contract\n165\t\n166\t**Census mandate (Slice C-0, before any fold code):** enumerate ALL ~30 `iter_records()`/`entries()` call sites and classify each `{windowed since_seq=cursor → prune-safe | monotonic security-bearer → MUST fold | content → MUST route to Q5}`. This is required because \"~9\" is provably incomplete.\n167\t\n168\t`SnapshotState.load(store)` reads the snapshot record **named strictly by the committed `head.snapshot_seq`** (empty identity state when the head is v1 / `snapshot_seq == -1` — an uncommitted/orphan snapshot record is inert). Every folding consumer switches to `st = SnapshotState.load(store); fold(st, [r for r in store.iter_records() if r.seq >= head.base_seq])`. Because both the fold-seed and the live-scan floor derive from the **same signed head**, they flip together at the commit instant — no double-count in any crash window. **Multi-prune:** each snapshot's `folded_state = fold(SnapshotState.load(prior_snapshot), delta_records[K_prev..K))`; all folds are associative (max / union / last-write / count-add / boundary-latch), so this is exact and never rescans from genesis. Seed an **empty** snapshot first (Slice C) and prove `fold == pure-scan` byte-identical *before any deletion*; extend to a two-prune `fold-of-fold == full-scan` proof.\n169\t\n170\t| # | Bearer (consumer) | Folds (over pruned `[0..K)`) | Fail direction if missed |\n171\t|---|---|---|---|\n172\t| 1 | `envelope.device_nonce_highwater` | `{device_pubkey: max(nonce)}` (semilattice, split-exact) | replay — **critical**, mandatory |\n173\t| 2 | warden checkpoint (`cli.py`/dashboard) | `{pubkey: [best_count, best_head_hash]}` highest anchored per key | anti-rollback regress |\n174\t| 3 | `killswitch._scan_engaged` | `engaged: bool` = the verified latch state at `K-1` (engage=any, release=owner-signed-verified, in order); ambiguous → `True` | fail-safe halt |\n175\t| 4 | `actor_scope.creation_allowed` | **`{(service,origin): count}` PAIR-keyed** of applied `account.create` in `[0..K)`; consumer `n = sum(c for (s,o),c in st if s==S or o==O) + live` | flat `{service}/{origin}` under-counts the OR-predicate → cap reset → **FATAL false-clean**; pair-key is split-exact |\n176\t| 5 | `mesh.authorized_devices` + `capability_map` | `{device_pubkey: authorized|revoked}` and `{host_id: cap}` latest-VERIFIED (owner-signed only) at `K-1`; snapshot MUST carry **every** key's state, consumer overlays live | dropped `revoked` re-authorizes — **critical** |\n177\t| 6 | `promotion.is_promoted` | `{\"agent\\x00scope\": granted|revoked}` latest-verified at `K-1` | dropped `revoked` re-grants auto-approval |\n178\t| 7 | `approvals.pending` | set of resolved `target_seq < K`; **assert** (referential floor guarantees no open pair straddles the boundary) | over-restrict (safe) |\n179\t| 8 | `revise` archivist current-view | the non-superseded-at-`K-1` archivist records **with full fields** — `supersedes_id, subject, quote, statement, grounding, alpha, beta, source_seqs, verified_seqs, conflicting_seqs, resolved, due_iso, owner, promotion_key` — so `queries.py` open_threads/due_commitments/**pending_contradictions** reconstruct identically; **+** `grounded_keys`/`refused_keys` idempotency SET-union | dropped `conflicting_seqs`/`verified_seqs` silently strips actionable contradictions/citations with **no verify() signal** — heaviest, needs a dedicated `iter_current` equivalence test |\n180\t| 9a | `gesture/session` device-arm `(device_pubkey, nonce)` **replay ledger** (HID-injection gate) | fold the consumed-nonce set **OR** assert-and-test `ARM_FRESHNESS << retention` (a prunable arm can never be replayed) | HID-injection replay — **critical**, do not leave implicit |\n181\t| 9b | `governor/budget` per-UTC-day cap | assert-and-test retention always keeps the current UTC day live (no fold needed) | cap reset |\n182\t\n183\t`queries.py` open threads/commitments/contradictions are a VIEW over #8 → covered. **Supersession needs no separate fold** (`supersedes_id` is forward-only). Graph/dashboard totals route to Q5 (§8), not silently shrink.\n184\t\n185\t---\n186\t\n187\t## 7. Referential integrity + prune-point guards\n188\t\n189\tRead-only under the flock BEFORE any write; any failure ABORTS the whole prune (no bytes touched):\n190\t\n191\t- **(a) Dangling parent/supersedes:** scan retained `[K..T]`; if any `parent_id`/`supersedes_id < K` is UNRESOLVED (not collapsed by the archivist fold and not recoverable from the archive), refuse. A dangling ref into *closed* history is benign (`resolve()→PrunedRef`); an *open-workflow* one blocks.\n192\t- **(b) Oldest-open-workflow floor:** `K ≤ min(seq)` over every open loop — `pending()` unresolved approval targets + their proposals, `queries` open threads/due commitments + cited `source_seqs`, unresolved contradictions, any operator plan/preview lacking its execute/verify. Every open workflow and everything it references stays live. This is what makes bearer #7 an assertion.\n193\t- **(c) Never mutate a retained binding:** the re-base rewrites zero record bytes; `base_prev_hash` equals the already-stored `prev_hash` of seq `K`, so no `prev_hash`/`parent_id`/`supersedes_id`/`entry_hash` is ever altered.\n194\t- **(d)** `K` aligns to a sealed-segment `first_seq` (whole segments only).\n195\t\n196\t---\n197\t\n198\t## 8. Q5 honest resolve\n199\t\n200\t`get(seq)` keeps its `SpineRecord | None` signature (hot path byte-identical); `None` is reserved for genuinely-never-existed (`seq < 0` or `seq > tip`). Add:\n201\t```python\n202\tresolve(seq) -> SpineRecord | PrunedRef\n203\tPrunedRef = frozen{pruned=True, seq, base_seq, snapshot_seq, cumulative_merkle_root, archive_hint}\n204\t```\n205\t`seq >= base_seq` → live `get()`. `0 <= seq < base_seq` → if the archive is mounted, `get_archived(seq)` (via `archive.manifest` `first_seq/last_seq` range → owning segment → gunzip → return the byte-identical `SpineRecord`, verified against the segment chain **and** a Merkle inclusion proof against `cumulative_merkle_root`); else `PrunedRef`, never a bare `None`. Migrate the old-seq resolvers (`actor_gate`, `actor`, `operator`, `perception/egress`, `bridge /api/record`, `ui /api/record`, `mcp episodic_range`, `consolidate/gate.py`, `transcript` parent_id) to `resolve()` → HTTP `410 Gone` with `{base_seq, snapshot_seq, \"attach archive/ or run sigil archive fetch <seq>\"}`, never a misleading `404`. **`episodic_range` with `since_seq < base_seq` returns the live tail PLUS a `PrunedRef` boundary marker** — an honest range, never silent truncation. Graph rebuild / dashboard totals surface the \"compacted below N\" marker too.\n206\t\n207\t---\n208\t\n209\t## 9. Crash-safe cutover — singular commit, forward-only reconciler\n210\t\n211\tAll coordination under the path-stable flock; the O(file) archive copy is **lock-free** on immutable sealed segments.\n212\t\n213\t**PHASE A (durable, reversible; nothing observable changes — live head is still the prior head over the full set):**\n214\t- **A0** Acquire flock. Choose `K` (segment-aligned). Run §7 guards. Compute `delta_merkle_root`, `cumulative_merkle_root`, and `folded_state = fold(load(prior), delta)`.\n215\t- **A1** Write `prune.intent` (fsync): `{K, base_seq, base_prev_hash, base_count, snapshot_seq, archived_segment_ids, delta_merkle_root, cumulative_merkle_root}` — the durable idempotency driver, written **before** the snapshot append.\n216\t- **A2** Append the `kind=\"snapshot\"` record (normal retain-all append → **fsync+ack**). Durable, nothing pruned yet.\n217\t- **A3** *(lock-free)* Copy the archived segments → `archive/segments/`, append `archive.manifest.json`, fsync each + dir-fsync; re-hash-verify every `sha256` and that the archive re-attaches (`boundary_hash == base_prev_hash`). **The pruned prefix is a complete, verified genesis→K-1 chain in the archive before any live drop.**\n218\t- **A4** Sign v2 head `H2` over the live window `[K..S]`; atomic-write to **`head.json.next` (staging — NOT live)**.\n219\t\n220\t**PHASE B (commit + idempotent reclaim; re-acquire flock):**\n221\t- **B1** `os.replace(head.json.next → head.json)`. **← THE COMMIT INSTANT.** After it, both verify (by-seq window) and every fold (seed keyed to `head.snapshot_seq`, scan floored at `head.base_seq`) see the pruned state — regardless of manifest membership.\n222\t- **B2** Advance `floor.json` upward (monotonic, meta-chain: `head_sig_hash := sha256(signing_bytes(H2))`).\n223\t- **B3** Re-read the manifest **fresh under the held flock**; new live set = `fresh.segments − archived_segment_ids` (set-difference — safe because a concurrent seal-swap only ADDS segments); atomic manifest re-base (`generation++`), set `base_*` advisory fields.\n224\t- **B4** Move the now-unreferenced archived originals to `trash/` (reader-grace) then unlink; dir-fsync. — physical reclaim.\n225\t- **B5** Delete `prune.intent`.\n226\t\n227\t**Why B1 is the singular commit:** live-scan pruning and fold-seeding are BOTH gated on the signed head (`base_seq` floor + `snapshot_seq` key), not on manifest membership — so they flip together at B1. B3/B4 are pure reclamation. This closes the double-count window that sank HARD-PRUNE's crash score.\n228\t\n229\t**RECONCILER (at open AND on every flock acquisition):** if `prune.intent` exists, re-drive idempotently from on-disk state — if `head.json.next` is a valid v2 head matching the intent, forward-complete B1→B5; else (Phase-A crash, head still prior) discard `head.json.next` and the intent (the orphan snapshot record is inert because no committed head names its `snapshot_seq`). Orphan archived originals not in the re-based manifest are GC'd like the existing seal orphan-GC. Set derivation is **manifest-only, never a directory glob**. If the owner key is unavailable (read-only verifier), stay in fail-safe TAMPER and report \"prune in progress — run `sigil sign`\", never false-clean.\n230\t\n231\t**No-lost-ack proof:** the snapshot record is fsync-acked before commit; every pruned record is in the verified archive (A3) before the live manifest drops it (B3) and before any unlink (B4); a crash at any barrier leaves each acked record either still live (`pre-B3`) or in the archive (`post-A3`). **No-false-tamper proof:** by-seq selection makes `(prior head + full manifest)`, `(v2 head + full manifest)`, and `(v2 head + re-based manifest)` all verify clean; there is no reachable valid state that reads as TAMPERING. **No panic-block:** the archive copy is off-lock, so a kill-switch PANIC append is never blocked (D1). **Kill-9 crash-fuzz at each A/B barrier — asserting verify()-clean, no lost ack, no double-count (fold-equivalence, not just chain-clean), archive re-attaches — is a required Slice-E merge gate.**\n232\t\n233\t---\n234\t\n235\t## 10. Honest cold-verifier residual (C1)\n236\t\n237\tBecause the owner key is FS-resident on the host and NOT on the mirror, **a keyless mirror adversary cannot forge a prune that drops specific real records** — that needs the Ed25519 signature over `base_prev_hash/base_count/cumulative_merkle_root`. The only feasible keyless attack is **replay of a whole prior owner-signed `{spine, head, floor, snapshot}` tuple** — a genuine stale rollback, undetectable from data alone, fundamental to any prunable single-owner-key log, and **class-identical to today's single-file rollback — not widened**.\n238\t\n239\tCold-archive bounds it on two axes: **INTEGRITY** — a verifier handed the archive re-attaches `[0..K)+[K..]`, re-verifies from true genesis, and re-derives the Merkle accumulator from the real leaves (any single pruned record carries a Merkle inclusion proof); **FRESHNESS** — the durable external floor + `prev_head_hash` meta-chain, with the initial floor **and** the archive delivered over the authenticated WireGuard pairing channel, never the mirror. The exposure narrows to exactly one case: **a verifier that consumes only an untrusted mirror and never authenticates the floor even once** — for whom freshness (not integrity) is unprovable. Every other failure flags false-tamper. Do not overclaim: bounded, not eliminated. The archive is a **new hard availability dependency** for full-genesis verification (lose it → pruned prefix unrecoverable, only the commitment survives) — an explicit MAX-RECLAIM tradeoff to state to the operator.\n240\t\n241\t---\n242\t\n243\t## 11.
